record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: If f is a strictly ergodic C¹ diffeomorphism of a compact connected manifold, meaning that f is both minimal and uniquely ergodic, must its topological entropy be equal to 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture. The topological entropy of f equals 0.

artifact.status_search_result: A literature search did not locate a resolution of this specific conjecture. Smooth minimal diffeomorphisms with positive topological entropy are known (Herman's constructions), but these are not uniquely ergodic. The Berger–Turaev (2017–2019) resolution of "Herman's positive entropy conjecture" addresses a different statement (perturbations of the identity in symplectic dynamics) and does not settle the strictly-ergodic case. No source found that constructs a strictly ergodic C¹ diffeomorphism of a compact connected manifold with positive topological entropy, nor a proof that none exists; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture (Berger–Turaev)
status_evidence.snippet: In every neighbourhood of identity in the set of smooth symplectic diffeomorphisms of the 2-dimensional disc, there exists a diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy.
status_evidence.claim: This resolved Herman's positive-entropy conjecture about perturbations of the identity, a different statement from the strictly-ergodic entropy question.

status_evidence.title: Berger and Turaev's Proof of Herman's Conjecture of Positive Entropy
status_evidence.snippet: Exposition of Berger–Turaev's proof concerning area-preserving perturbations near elliptic fixed points.
status_evidence.claim: Concerns a distinct Herman conjecture; does not address whether strictly ergodic C¹ diffeomorphisms must have zero topological entropy.
